correctness.rationale: Independently re-verified all essential inferences. Ringel orientable genus ceil((4-2)(9-2)/4)=ceil(14/4)=4 is correct; Euler V-E+F=2-2g gives F=17 at g=4. Bipartiteness forces even faces; length-2 faces impossible in a simple graph with min degree >=2 because the successor in a cyclic rotation of length >=2 is a different edge, so all faces have even length >=4. Hence sum(l_i)=72 and sum(l_i-4)=4 with each excess even and >=0, forcing exactly partitions 4 and 2+2, i.e. S subset of {4^15,6^2} and {4^16,8^1}. Both witnesses were machine-verified by calling verify.py functions directly on inputs/artifacts/witnesses.json: witness A yields F=17, g=4, sorted lengths [4x15,6x2]; witness B yields F=17, g=4, [4x16,8]. The script checks rotation domains, dart partition (72 darts each once), double count sum=72, evenness/girth, and Euler genus. DRAFT rotation tables match witnesses.json entries, and listed face walks alternate across the bipartition. Section 3 is pure deduction; face tracing is computed evidence re-verifiable by hand or script under the stated successor convention.

originality.rationale: Fused retrieval over literal, equivalent-formulation, and dominance queries found no prior source recording or implying the exact K(4,9) minimum-genus face-multiset classification. The nearest face-distribution work (Sun, complete graphs K_n, arXiv:1708.02092) concerns a different graph family and does not cover complete bipartite K(4,9). Broader K_{m,n} genus literature (regular embeddings of K_{n,n} by Jones; counting by Shao-Liu-Li; Conder-Stokes methods; quadrangular embeddings of K_n) gives genus values, regular-case classifications, counts, or constructions but no complete face-size multiset theorem for K(4,9) and no table listing {4^15,6^2} and {4^16,8^1} as the realized set. Ringel genus formula plus Euler counting only imply S is a subset of the two candidates, not that both occur; realizability required new explicit rotation systems. No official database or census was found covering the claim as a special case.

value.rationale: TARGET route: the admitted target asked exactly for the complete set S with one explicit rotation system per multiset plus exclusion of all others, and the report delivers precisely that. Under the shared STANDARD, a rigorously established exact invariant of a specific natural object (here the two realized face-size multisets of minimum-genus orientable K(4,9), motivated before computation) is independently valuable without a new general theorem when the value is not known or mechanically implied and a future researcher could need the precise fact. Both conditions hold: Euler arithmetic leaves two candidates but does not imply either is realizable, and the two genus-4 rotation-system witnesses are non-trivial constructions a future worker on bipartite embeddings, quadrangulation obstructions, or rotation-system benchmarks could reasonably retrieve. This is not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny gain, or unexplained enumeration.
